targets.forbidden_identifiers: The lineage id and every identifier derived from it: its versions, representations, sections, chunks, claims, mentions, cross-references, testimony-currency events, the entity whose only provenance it was, and the fact whose only evidence lineage it was.
targets.mutation: Set documents.deleted_at on the fixture lineage.
targets.summary: A live document lineage is forgotten.

targets.forbidden_identifiers: The version id and every identifier derived from it: its representation, sections, chunks, claims, and mentions. The facts those claims evidenced keep their surviving historical provenance and are deliberately not forbidden.
targets.mutation: Set document_versions.deleted_at on the fixture version.
targets.summary: One non-current version of a live lineage is tombstoned.

targets.forbidden_identifiers: The superseded representation id and the sections and chunks cut from it. The fixture lineage carries no claims, so no testimony legitimately outlives the reading and the forbidden set stays global.
targets.mutation: Insert a new ready representation, point the version's current representation at it, and leave the previous reading in place.
targets.summary: The current ready reading of a live version is superseded.

targets.forbidden_identifiers: The claim id. The fact it evidenced keeps its association row and stays visible with a reduced count, which is the D54 behaviour rather than a leak.
targets.mutation: Delete the claim row and its chunk occurrences.
targets.summary: One claim is purged from the testimony record.

targets.forbidden_identifiers: The fact id, which must disappear from the fact relations, the evidence bridge, the contradiction and graph projections, and the change feed.
targets.mutation: Delete the fact's relation or observation evidence rows.
targets.summary: Every evidence lineage of one fact is removed.

targets.forbidden_identifiers: The cited lineage id, its derived identifiers, and the chunk content hashes that locate the cited claims. The citing page keeps its other citations and stays visible; only the citation of the forgotten lineage leaves, which is what proves a chunk-content hash locator cannot authorize a read on its own.
targets.mutation: Set documents.deleted_at on the cited lineage.
targets.summary: The lineage a knowledge page cites is forgotten.

targets.forbidden_identifiers: Every nominated identifier and body byte whose PostgreSQL coordinate no longer confirms, which the in-function confirmation must drop and count.
targets.mutation: Delete the nominated chunk, claim, or entity behind a frozen P1 candidate set, then run the semantic and lexical functions.
targets.summary: A stale P1 nomination candidate is deleted from PostgreSQL.

targets.forbidden_identifiers: The relation identifier after its last surviving evidence row is deleted; no graph generation or stale snapshot exception exists.
targets.mutation: Delete the surviving evidence behind a relation, then read the live graph authorities in the same transaction.
targets.summary: A live graph edge loses its last surviving evidence row.

targets.forbidden_identifiers: Every byte of the forgotten body and every hash that would confirm it, across the id-addressed body fetch and the corpus filesystem.
targets.mutation: Hard-forget the content object behind a chunk, then fetch that chunk's body by id.
targets.summary: The body bytes behind a live chunk coordinate are forgotten.
